purpose: Determine whether the frozen robust BEDROC20 receptor-set utility contains reproducible greedy traps, pairwise-closed structure, or stable higher-order residuals before designing another QUBO objective.

diagnostic.set_utility: equal-weight mean of primary BEDROC20, mean-seed BEDROC20, and worst-seed BEDROC20
diagnostic.greedy_definition: Start from the best singleton under the training set utility and add the receptor giving the highest resulting set utility at every cardinality; break ties lexicographically.
diagnostic.legacy_greedy_comparator: Separately reproduce the prior direct_greedy lexicographic rule ordered by worst-seed BEDROC20, primary BEDROC20, mean-seed BEDROC20, primary PR-AUC, and primary ROC-AUC.
diagnostic.exact_definition: Enumerate every receptor subset at each cardinality and select the highest training set utility; break ties lexicographically.
diagnostic.pairwise_closure: For each triple, predict utility as the sum of its three observed pair utilities minus the sum of its three singleton utilities plus one least-squares intercept fitted over all triples.
diagnostic.third_order_residual: Observed triple utility minus the pairwise-closure prediction.
diagnostic.submodularity_check: Enumerate all pairwise diminishing-return inequalities with nonempty source sets of size one through four; separately enumerate every marginal edge through size six to measure nonmonotonicity.

route_gate.decision_boundary: A target is a pairwise-closure QUBO candidate only when k=3 has a reproducible greedy gap and pairwise top-tail fidelity passes. It is an auxiliary or higher-order candidate only when at least two cardinalities have reproducible greedy gaps, pairwise fidelity fails, and triple residuals are stable across outer training folds. Mixed target routes do not authorize a cross-target efficacy QUBO.

interpretation_boundary: Stage 19g is a post-hoc mathematical diagnostic over MK14 and PPARG training matrices whose outcomes are already known. It adds no docking and reads no BACE1 docking, fresh-validation, or test row. It may choose the representation class for one subsequent train-only development stage, but it cannot amend BACE1, alter prior failures, establish cross-target QUBO superiority, demonstrate quantum execution, or establish quantum advantage.
